chunks: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام was asked about what is extracted from the sea, such as pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and about mines of gold and silver: is there zakat on them?
He said: “If its value reaches one dinar, then khums is due on it.”

key_terms.الزَّبَرْجَدِ: emerald or green precious stone taken from the sea
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax due on qualifying extracted wealth
key_terms.الْيَاقُوتِ: ruby, a precious stone mentioned among sea extractions
key_terms.دِينَاراً: the monetary threshold mentioned for liability
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: obligatory alms-tax being asked about in the question
key_terms.مَعَادِنِ: mines or mineral sources from which wealth is extracted

ai.seo_question: When does khums become obligatory on minerals and treasures extracted from the sea?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding wealth extracted from the sea and from mines, such as pearls, rubies, emeralds, gold, and silver. Imam Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام states that when its value reaches one dinar, khums becomes due on it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1644 - Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) was asked about what is extracted from the sea, such as pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and about mines of gold and silver: "Is there Zakat on them?"
Imam (as) replied: "If their value reaches one dinar, then Khums (one-fifth) is due on them."
